new_this_week.title: The Boroughs
new_this_week.about: Eight-episode sci-fi/horror executive-produced by the Duffer Brothers (Stranger Things). In a picturesque retirement community, an unlikely band of heroes — Geena Davis, Alfred Molina, Bill Pullman, Alfre Woodard, Clarke Peters, Denis O'Hare, Jena Malone — face an otherworldly threat that's stealing the one thing they don't have: time. Created by Jeffrey Addiss and Will Matthews. All 8 episodes drop together.
new_this_week.why: Sci-fi + supernatural + ensemble + Stranger Things pedigree is a direct multi-signal match — and a full-season binge, not a weekly wait. The most anticipated new series of the week behind the The Boys finale.

new_this_week.title: Widow's Bay — Ep 5 'What to Expect on Your Trip'
new_this_week.about: Episode 5 of the 10-episode small-town supernatural mystery from Katie Dippold (Parks and Rec writer), with Hiro Murai directing and Matthew Rhys as the mayor of a cursed New England island town. Ep 5's trailer teases a new horror threat.
new_this_week.why: Pinned, and you rated Ep 4 a 4⭐ ('ensemble, magic, suspense, supernatural'). Stay-current midweek bedtime pick — same slot as last week.

new_this_week.title: Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed
new_this_week.about: Tatiana Maslany leads a darkly comedic thriller as newly divorced mom Paula, who spirals into blackmail, murder, and youth-soccer politics during a custody battle and identity crisis. Created by David J. Rosen. Two-episode premiere today, then weekly through Jul 15.
new_this_week.why: Dark comedy + 30-min episodes + a strong lead lines up with your Fleabag / Solar Opposites / Slow Horses shelf. Maslany is a credibility anchor, and the half-hour runtime fits the bedtime window.

new_this_week.title: Nope (2022)
new_this_week.about: Jordan Peele's 2022 sci-fi/horror — siblings OJ and Emerald Haywood (Daniel Kaluuya, Keke Palmer) run a California horse ranch and discover something hovering above it. 83% RT, $171M global box office. Left Peacock for a Netflix-exclusive run.
new_this_week.why: Two of your top genres in one (sci-fi + horror/suspense). Peele delivers plot twists that pay off and elevated horror with substance underneath — squarely your hit signal. Newly on a platform you're on.

new_this_week.title: Devil May Cry S2
new_this_week.about: Adi Shankar's adult-animation series based on the Capcom franchise. Season 2 launches the Dante–Vergil rivalry; all 8 episodes are out. Season 1 hit 96% RT in 2025 and debuted in Netflix's Top 10.
new_this_week.why: Adult animation + supernatural + 30-min episodes — the same shelf as Solar Opposites. The highest-pedigree binge sitting on your platforms right now.

new_this_week.title: Black Phone 2
new_this_week.about: Scott Derrickson's sequel to 2021's The Black Phone. Finney and Gwen face The Grabber (Ethan Hawke) again — this time through dreams. $132M box office, 82% RT audience score. Begins a 10-month Netflix-exclusive run. R-rated.
new_this_week.why: Horror/suspense sits in your top-4 genre stack — a Saturday-night bedtime horror option. Note critics were harder on it than the first film, so it's a strong-genre-fit, lighter-on-acclaim pick.

new_this_week.title: Lord of the Flies
new_this_week.date: Streaming since Mon May 4, 2026 (4-ep limited series)
new_this_week.about: Jack Thorne's 4-part adaptation of Golding's novel, directed by Marc Munden. Certified Fresh at 92% RT — critics called it 'influential, hypnotic, and witty.' The IMDB audience score sits notably lower (~6.7).
new_this_week.why: Try, not strong. Book adaptation + a tight 4-ep run is your signal, but the critic/audience gap and heavy stylization make Ep 1 a probe, not a commitment.

new_this_week.title: Mating Season
new_this_week.about: From the Big Mouth creative team (Nick Kroll, Mark Levin, Jennifer Flackett, Andrew Goldberg). Anthropomorphic forest critters — a bear voiced by Zach Woods and a raccoon voiced by Kroll — navigate mating-season hookups. 6-episode first season.
new_this_week.why: Adult animation + ~25-min eps is your shelf on paper. Try-flag — Big Mouth's juvenile-leaning humor sits on your miss-signal list. One-episode probe to see whether it skews adult-witty or kid-raunchy.

new_this_week.title: Ladies First
new_this_week.about: A high-concept comedy: ad-agency exec Damien Sachs (Sacha Baron Cohen) wakes up in a parallel world dominated by women and goes head-to-head with Alex Fox (Rosamund Pike), a once-overlooked employee. Directed by Thea Sharrock; ensemble includes Richard E. Grant, Emily Mortimer, Charles Dance, Fiona Shaw. An English-language remake of the French film 'I Am Not an Easy Man.'
new_this_week.why: Comedy is a top genre and the cast is strong. Try-flag — Baron Cohen's broad comic register can run against your dry/witty preference, and there's no critic score pre-release. Sample it if the premise lands.
